facts.text: During the American Revolution, Wallkill’s factories in Phillipsburgh and Craigville produced gunpowder for the Continental Army, thanks to Henry Wisner and Moses Phillips.
Wallkill sits just east of the dramatic Shawangunk Ridge, a landmark that shapes the Hudson Valley’s natural scenery.
Wallkill’s history stretches back to 1724, but the town wasn’t officially established until 1772, just before Ulster County split off.
The town proudly hosts the first Lloyd’s Supercenter in New York, a retail milestone that once drew shoppers from across the state.
Every summer, Wallkill opens its gates for the Orange County Fair, a long‑running event that showcases local culture and agriculture.
Wallkill’s downtown once housed the first mall in the area, Orange Plaza, before the modern Galleria at Crystal Run and a Super Wal‑Mart took over.
